title: Strategy-to-Sprint Conduit: cross-functional gating spec for company-level OKRs
creator: Morgan Reyes
description: Problem: Company-level OKRs are currently translated to engineering and GTM deliverables unevenly across teams; this causes scope creep, misaligned milestones, and missed gates during releases. Goal: Define a clear "strategy-to-sprint" conduit that prescribes how an OKR becomes a prioritized set of initiatives, how gates are defined and enforced, and what telemetry and decision rights are required across Eng/PM/Design/Sales. Scope: 1) Create gating taxonomy (concept, design, build, rollout) and pass/fail criteria; 2) Define RACI for decisions at each gate and for cross-team escalations; 3) Publish templates (initiative brief, acceptance checklist, rollout playbook); 4) Wire a lightweight tracking surface in the Console roadmap dashboard; 5) Run a dry-run with two pilot initiatives (Dedicated autoscaling policies + Console rollout observability). Out of scope: deep implementation of tooling integrations (will be follow-up with ENG tickets). Deliverables: PRD, gating spec, initiative templates, dashboard prototype, pilot retro and adoption plan.
acceptance_criteria: All company-level OKRs are mapped to at least one initiative with owner and estimated milestones
Gating taxonomy (concept/design/build/rollout) documented with concrete pass/fail criteria for each gate
Decision RACI matrix published and signed off by Eng, Product, Design, and GTM leads
Initiative brief and rollout checklist templates available in Confluence and referenced from linear tickets
Console roadmap dashboard shows first-pass tracking for pilot initiatives (latency/cost/uptime slices)
Pilot initiatives complete dry-run and retro, with a concrete adoption plan and next-step ENG tickets created
